themes_detail.label: Dead trees spiking this week
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—suggesting either rapid environmental deterioration, storm damage, or a newly visible problem in Far Rockaway's green space.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
Long-standing community board budget request for park reconstruction and new green space amenities suggests chronic under-investment in tree maintenance
Timing coincides with potential post-storm assessment or seasonal die-off
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about tree health assessments in Far Rockaway and maintenance schedules
Visit affected blocks to document visible tree damage and canopy loss; identify common cause (storm, disease, neglect)

themes_detail.label: Water quality crisis emerging
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints hit 3 THREE WEEKS AGO, representing a 2300% spike from a near-zero 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical severity recorded)—the most extreme deviation in the dataset, warranting immediate investigation into potential contamination or infrastructure failure.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest severity in data)
Long-standing community board budget request for DEP capital projects and sanitary sewer development in specific street segments suggests known infrastructure gaps
Related: 283 water system complaints over 90 days indicates chronic water infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP water quality test results and complaint details from 3 weeks ago; identify affected neighborhoods
Interview residents about discolored water, taste/odor issues; cross-reference with DEP maintenance records and aging pipe infrastructure

themes_detail.label: Damaged street signs proliferating
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped to 17 LAST WEEK versus a 3.1 weekly average (444% spike, z-score: 7.87)—suggesting either a localized weather event, vehicular collision cluster, or deferred maintenance crisis affecting navigation and safety.
evidence: 17 street sign–damaged complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (444% increase, z-score: 7.87)
Concurrent spike in street light condition complaints (27 last week vs. 13.5 avg) suggests broader street infrastructure failure
1,036 street condition complaints over 90 days indicates systemic road maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Map the 17 damaged sign reports to identify geographic cluster or corridor; determine common damage pattern (impact, weather, vandalism)
Interview DOT about sign replacement timelines and whether weather or traffic event preceded the spike

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise surge last week
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 11 LAST WEEK from a 3.6 weekly baseline (203% spike, z-score: 3.69)—potentially signaling new construction activity, business expansion, or venue operations coinciding with active 422 building permits filed in the past 90 days.
evidence: 11 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (203% increase, z-score: 3.69)
422 active DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (236 alterations, 156 new buildings) indicate heavy construction activity that may drive noise
Concurrent residential noise issue remains highest-volume complaint type (1,250 over 90 days), suggesting noise tolerance is low
reporting_angles: Cross-reference commercial noise complaints with active construction permits to identify specific projects or business locations driving surge
Interview affected residents in blocks with highest noise complaints; determine if complaints target specific venues, construction sites, or delivery operations

themes_detail.label: Street lighting gaps widening
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints doubled to 27 LAST WEEK from a 13.5 weekly baseline (100% spike, z-score: 3.52)—potentially linked to aging infrastructure, storm damage, or a maintenance backlog that mirrors long-standing community board requests for capital projects.
evidence: 27 street light condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (100% increase, z-score: 3.52)
Parallels spike in street sign damage (17 last week vs. 3.1 avg) suggesting broader street infrastructure failure event
Repeated community board budget requests for capital projects imply chronic under-investment in public space maintenance
reporting_angles: Request Con Edison and DOE outage/maintenance logs for last 2–3 weeks to identify weather event or systemic failure
Document dark blocks at night and interview residents about safety concerns; assess whether lights are burned out, vandalized, or damaged
